images: The threshold where architecture meets light. This residence in Montería captures the precise moment when concrete surrenders to warmth.
Pietra serena and flowing water. The courtyard becomes a vessel for reflection—literal and metaphorical.
Compression and release. The entry narrows, then expands into the landscape. A choreography of movement.
Board-formed concrete holds the memory of its making. Timber screens filter the tropical sun.
Water announces the threshold. The guest crosses a mirror pond before touching land.
Hernando Carrillo in the studio. 38 years of drawings, models, and built work behind him.
Architecture reveals its second self at night. Light becomes material; shadow becomes space.
Carrara marble, volcanic stone, oak. The daily ritual elevated to ceremony.
Floor-to-ceiling glass dissolves the boundary. The landscape becomes the artwork.
Where steel meets stone meets glass. The detail is not decoration—it is the idea made visible.
The garden is not around the house. The house is in the garden. Native species, zero irrigation.
Light wells penetrate three floors. The section is the generator; the plan follows.
Overhangs calculated to the solar path. Cross-ventilation in every room. No mechanical cooling.
Five years post-occupancy. The patina of time improves the work. Architecture ages; bad design decays.
Grasshopper definitions driving facade optimization. 400 iterations to find the one.
The project begins with water. Where it falls, where it flows, where it reflects. Everything follows.
The napkin sketch that became a 2,500m² cultural center. The idea survives the process.
Sun path, wind rose, thermal mass, evaporative cooling. The section as climate machine.
3D-printed base, VR walkthrough, hand-crafted details. The hybrid workflow.
The land dictates. We listen. The building sits where the slope breathes.
37 materials approved. Each with provenance, carbon data, aging behavior.
Local masons, digital layout. The tolerance is 2mm. The humanity is infinite.
